svg.text: The route with the fewest firms is the least concentrated of them all

hands

The vertical rule is the largest tenth of a route's firms; the dots are where each
curve crosses it and the panel beside reads them off. The closer a curve runs to
the dashed diagonal, the more evenly the work is shared; routes drawn faintly in
the panel are omitted here to keep the plot legible and are otherwise identical.
and the same thing as one number

firms
top 10%
Deep-well is last on this list and first on a count of firms.
A route can be scarce and fairly shared, or crowded and owned
by one company: other treatment has 77 firms and 86% of it is
Ascend Performance Materials' Chocolate Bayou plant, which
with its deep-well tonnage is 17% of every ton managed in
America.
2023 cycle, managed_tons on GM and WR rows which do not overlap. Both axes are normalised within the route, so a route with 31 firms and one with 367
are comparable. handler_id is a facility, not a company: names are normalised to an owner first, which takes Clean Harbors' 21 sites to one firm. An
earlier version of this figure plotted firm count against share of national tonnage, which measures average firm size rather than concentration and
ranked deep-well first instead of last. Method and limits in the recipe README.
